phaseFocus.1: Pain/inflammation control, quad activation, basic ROM

1.name: Quad Sets
steps: Lie on your back on the floor
Straighten your injured leg
Push the back of your knee into the floor by tightening your quad
Hold for 2 seconds, release, repeat
1.feel: You should feel your quad muscle tighten and burn on top of your thigh.

1.name: Heel Props
steps: Place a rolled towel or foam roller under your heel
Put a light weight (2-5 lbs) on your thigh just above the knee
Relax your leg completely and let gravity straighten it
Hold for 5 minutes total, relax and breathe
1.feel: You should feel a gentle stretch in the back of your knee and calf. The quad is fully relaxed.

1.name: Heel Slides
steps: Lie on your back with legs straight
Slowly slide your heel toward your buttock, bending your knee
Hold at maximum bend for 3 seconds
Slowly slide back to starting position
1.feel: You should feel your hamstring engage as you slide, and a gentle stretch in the knee.

1.name: Straight Leg Raises
steps: Lie on your back, one leg bent with foot flat
Keep your injured leg completely straight
Tighten your quad and lift the leg to the height of the opposite bent knee
Lower slowly—take 3 seconds down, don't drop
1.feel: You should feel your quad working hard on top of your thigh. No pain in the knee.

1.name: Glute Bridges
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on floor hip-width apart
Push through your heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling
Squeeze your glutes at the top—hips should be fully elevated
Lower slowly back down, maintain glute engagement
1.feel: You should feel your glutes and hamstrings working. Lower back stays comfortable.

1.name: Clamshells
steps: Lie on your side with knees bent 90°, feet together
Place a band around both thighs just above the knees
Keep your feet touching—rotate your top knee upward like opening a clam
Control the return—don't let the band snap your legs back
1.feel: You should feel a burn in your outer hip and glute. Keep core braced to prevent rolling.

1.name: Hamstring Curls
steps: Lie face down with a resistance band around your ankle
Secure the band under your opposite foot or to a fixed point
Curl your heel toward your buttock, bending the knee
Lower slowly and with control—3 seconds down
1.feel: You should feel the back of your thigh working. Keep hips pressed to the floor.

2.name: Quad Sets
steps: Lie on your back on the floor
Straighten your injured leg completely
Tighten your quad hard—press the back of your knee down
Hold 2 seconds, fully release, repeat without rest between reps
2.feel: You should feel your quad muscle squeeze hard on top of your thigh.

2.name: Heel Slides
steps: Start with legs straight, lie on your back
Slide heel toward buttock, bending knee fully
Hold bent position for 3 seconds at peak contraction
Slide back to straight leg slowly—take 3 seconds
2.feel: You should feel hamstring engagement on the slide back, knee flexion stretch.

2.name: Straight Leg Raises
steps: Lie on your back, uninjured leg bent with foot planted
Injured leg stays straight, quad tight
Lift leg to the height of your bent knee—lead with the heel
Lower in 3 seconds—no swinging, no dropping
2.feel: You should feel quad fatigue building. Controlled, smooth movement only.

2.name: Short Arc Quads
steps: Place a foam roller or rolled towel under your knee
With knee resting on the roll, straighten your leg
Lift heel so only the back of your knee touches the roll
Hold at full extension for 2 seconds, lower slowly
2.feel: You should feel quad engagement through a partial range—gentle on the knee.

2.name: Glute Bridges
steps: Lie on back, feet flat, knees bent, arms relaxed
Drive through heels—lift hips until body forms a straight line
Squeeze glutes hard at the top—hold 1 second
Lower in 2-3 seconds, maintain tension throughout
2.feel: You should feel glutes working hard. Back should stay neutral, no arching.

2.name: Clamshells
steps: Side-lying with knees bent 90°, feet together, band around thighs
Keep feet touching—rotate top knee upward without rolling back
Lift knee as high as possible while maintaining position
Lower slowly against band resistance—3 seconds
2.feel: You should feel outer hip and glute burn. Core stays braced, no back rolling.

2.name: Single Leg Bridges
steps: Lie on back, one knee bent with foot flat, other leg straight
Push through the planted foot to lift hips
Extend fully at top—body forms straight line on bent leg side
Lower slowly, maintain control throughout
2.feel: You should feel glute and hamstring working harder on one side. Core engaged.

2.name: Terminal Knee Extensions
steps: Sit with band anchored behind you, loop around front of shin
Knee bent at 90°, pull band to straighten leg
Fully straighten, squeeze quad at full extension
Return to 90° slowly—resist the band on the way back
2.feel: You should feel quad working through the last 45° of extension.

3.name: Single Leg Bridges
steps: Lie on back, one foot planted, opposite leg straight in air
Lift hips by driving through the planted heel
At the top, your body should form a straight line from shoulders to extended foot
Hold 3 seconds at top, lower with control—4 seconds down
3.feel: You should feel intense glute burn on the working side. Core braced tight.

3.name: Clamshells
steps: Side-lying, knees bent, band around thighs
Feet stay together—open top knee against resistance
Go slow on the way up, even slower on the way down
Don't let your hip roll back or body twist
3.feel: You should feel hip abductor fatigue building. Steady, controlled movement.

3.name: Standing Hip Abduction
steps: Stand tall, band around both ankles
Lift one leg out to the side—lead with the heel
Keep standing leg slightly bent, don't lean
Lower slowly and with control—don't drop the leg
3.feel: You should feel outer hip and glute working. Standing leg stays strong.

3.name: Mini Squats
steps: Stand in front of a counter or wall for support
Feet hip-width apart, toes forward
Bend knees slightly and push hips back—like sitting in a chair
Only go down 3-4 inches—stand back up, stay upright
3.feel: You should feel quad and glute engagement. Knee tracks over toes.

3.name: Step Ups
steps: Use a low step (4-6 inches), stand facing it
Step up with your injured leg first
Drive through the heel, fully straighten at the top
Step down with control—don't bounce or slam
3.feel: You should feel quad and glute working. Control the descent slowly.

3.name: Single Leg Stance
steps: Stand on your injured leg near a wall for safety
Slightly bend the standing knee, engage the glute
Arms can be at sides or for balance
Progress by closing eyes or adding head turns
3.feel: You should feel ankle and hip stabilizing. Core stays tight.

3.name: Hamstring Slider
steps: Lie on back with heels on a smooth surface (sock on floor works)
Lift hips into a bridge position—heels near buttock
Slide heels away, extending legs while keeping hips up
Pull heels back to start—squeeze glutes throughout
3.feel: You should feel hamstring burn and glute engagement. Hips stay high.

3.name: Standing Calf Raises
steps: Stand facing a wall for balance, feet hip-width apart
Rise onto the balls of your feet—lift heels as high as possible
Hold at the top for 1 second
Lower slowly—take 3 seconds down, full stretch at bottom
3.feel: You should feel calf muscle tighten. Both legs, or focus on injured side.

4.name: Single Leg RDL
steps: Stand on injured leg, slight bend in the knee
Hinge at the hip—push your butt back while extending free leg behind
Keep your back flat, torso nearly parallel to the ground
Return to standing by squeezing glute and hamstring
4.feel: You should feel hamstring and glute working. Standing leg stays strong.

4.name: Split Squats
steps: Stand in a split stance—one foot forward, one back
Back heel elevated slightly on toes
Bend front knee, lower until back knee nearly touches floor
Push through front heel to return to start
4.feel: You should feel quad and glute working. Front knee tracks over toes.

4.name: Lateral Step Downs
steps: Stand on a low step (4-6 inches), injured leg on the edge
Slowly lower your other heel toward the floor
Keep your knee tracking over your toes—don't let it collapse inward
Push through the standing leg to return up
4.feel: You should feel quad working eccentrically. Knee stays stable.

4.name: Band Walks
steps: Place band around both ankles or above knees
Squat slightly—hinge hips back like sitting in a chair
Take 6-8 steps to one side, maintaining band tension
Reverse direction, come back to start
4.feel: You should feel outer hip and glute burn. Knees stay over toes.

4.name: Single Leg Bridge
steps: Lie on back, single leg extended
Drive through the grounded heel, lift hips high
Hold 3 seconds at the top with full hip extension
Lower slowly—glute stays engaged throughout
4.feel: You should feel glute fatigue building. Core stays tight.

4.name: Single Leg Calf Raises
steps: Stand on injured leg only, other leg bent behind
Rise up onto the ball of your foot as high as possible
Hold at the top for 1 second
Lower slowly for 3 seconds—full stretch at bottom
4.feel: You should feel calf working hard. Balance is challenging—hold wall.

4.name: Single Leg Stance
steps: Stand on injured leg, slight knee bend
Progress to standing on a pillow or cushion for instability
Close eyes, add head turns, or catch a ball
Maintain upright posture, core braced throughout
4.feel: You should feel ankle and hip stabilizers working hard. Balance challenged.

4.name: Cossack Squats
steps: Stand with feet wide apart, toes pointed out
Shift weight to one side, bending that knee deeply
Keep the other leg straight—heel down, toes up
Push through the bent leg to return, alternate sides
4.feel: You should feel inner thigh and quad working on the bent side.

5.name: Single Leg Squat
steps: Stand on injured leg in front of a box or chair
Extend other leg slightly forward for balance
Slowly lower yourself until you touch the box
Drive through your heel to stand back up—no pushing off the floor
5.feel: You should feel quad and glute working. Knee stays stable over toes.

5.name: Single Leg RDL
steps: Stand on injured leg holding a light dumbbell in opposite hand
Hinge at hips, extend free leg behind for balance
Keep back flat, torso nearly parallel to floor
Return to standing—squeeze glute at the top
5.feel: You should feel hamstring and glute working hard. Core braced tight.

5.name: Double Leg Jumps
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width, knees slightly bent
Jump up explosively, extend hips and knees fully
Land softly on the balls of your feet
Immediately jump again—minimize ground contact time
5.feel: You should feel powerful leg drive. Knees stay aligned, land soft.

5.name: Lateral Hops
steps: Stand sideways to a line or marker on the floor
Jump sideways over the line with both feet together
Land on the balls of your feet, absorb the impact
Jump back to the starting side immediately
5.feel: You should feel lateral quad and glute working. Land controlled.

5.name: Pogo Jumps
steps: Stand with feet together, knees slightly bent
Jump up rapidly, staying on the balls of your feet
Immediately spring back up—minimize time on the ground
Stay as high as possible with quick, reactive jumps
5.feel: You should feel calves and ankles working. Light, springy movement.

5.name: Single Leg Hops
steps: Stand on injured leg only
Jump forward—not far, focus on quality
Land on the same leg softly—absorb through knee and hip
Reset and repeat—focus on landing quality over distance
5.feel: You should feel power from your leg. Landing should feel controlled.

5.name: Carioca/Grapevine
steps: Stand sideways, step one foot in front of the other
Cross the back foot behind, then in front
Keep the rhythm going—walk sideways quickly
After 15 seconds, reverse direction
5.feel: You should feel hip flexibility and coordination. Core stays engaged.

5.name: Box Jumps
steps: Stand facing a low box (8-12 inches)
Jump explosively, driving knees up
Land softly on top of the box—both feet together
Step back down (don't jump down), reset, repeat
5.feel: You should feel powerful leg drive. Land soft, quiet on the box.

1.name: Stationary Bike
1.cue: Low resistance, focus on full pedal circle. Warm up.

1.name: Leg Press
1.cue: Only go to 45° knee bend. Focus on quad control.

1.name: Seated Hamstring Curls
1.cue: Control the eccentric. No jerky movements.

1.name: Cable Terminal Knee Ext
1.cue: 90° to 45° range. Squeeze quad at full extension.

1.name: Exercise Ball Curls
1.cue: Bridge up, roll ball with heels. Control the return.

1.name: Leg Extensions
1.cue: 90° to full extension. No pad pressure on shin.

2.name: Leg Press
2.cue: Deeper range now. Both legs, then single leg variations.

2.name: Seated Hamstring Curls
2.cue: Both legs, then single. Full range.

2.name: Goblet Squats
2.cue: Hold weight at chest. Keep chest up, knees out.

2.name: Step Ups
2.cue: Use low step. Drive through heel, not toes.

2.name: Prone Terminal Knee Ext
2.cue: Cable behind knee, lie prone. Extend fully.

2.name: Seated Calf Raises
2.cue: Full stretch at bottom, rise fully on toes.

3.name: Single Leg Press
3.cue: Focus on the injured leg. Full range.

3.name: Goblet Squats
3.cue: Deeper squat, heavier weight. Chest up.

3.name: Bulgarian Split Squats
3.cue: Back foot elevated on bench. Hold rack for balance.

3.name: Romanian Deadlifts
3.cue: Hinge at hips, keep bar close. Feel hamstrings.

3.name: Leg Extensions
3.cue: Slow and controlled. Full squeeze at top.

3.name: Hip Sled
3.cue: Focus on quad control through full range.

4.name: Back Squats
4.cue: Focus on form. Box squats for control.

4.name: Bulgarian Split Squats
4.cue: No hands. Full depth if possible.

4.name: Single Leg RDL
4.cue: Dumbbell in opposite hand. Hip hinge.

4.name: Nordic Curl Negatives
4.cue: Slow eccentric only. Catch with hands.

5.name: Back Squats
5.cue: Working sets. Focus on depth and form.

5.name: Deadlifts
5.cue: Conventional or sumo. Keep back neutral.
